The '''Wilkie investment model''', often just called '''Wilkie model''', is a [[stochastic asset model]] developed by A. D. Wilkie that describes the behavior of various economics factors as [[stochastic process|stochastic]] [[time series]]. These time series are generated by [[autoregressive model]]s. The main factor of the model which influences all asset prices is the [[consumer price index]]. The model is mainly in use for [[actuary|actuarial]] work and [[asset liability management]]. Because of the stochastic properties of that model it is mainly combined with [[Monte Carlo method]]s.

Wilkie first proposed the model in 1986, in a paper published in the ''Transactions of the Faculty of Actuaries''.<ref>

He advises to use that model to determine the "funnel of doubt", which can be seen as an interval of minimum and maximum development of a corresponding economic factor.

==Components==
* price inflation
* wage inflation
* share yield
* share dividend
* consols yield (long-term interest rate)
* bank rate (short-term interest rate)
